Rashi on Gittin 2b:1:1.hebrew: גמ'. לפי שאין בקיאין לשמה - אין בני מדינת הים בני תורה, ואין יודעין שצריך לכתוב הגט לשם האשה. וקרא כתיב "וכתב לה ספר כריתות" (דברים כ״ד:א׳) — "לה", דהיינו לשמה. הילכך אומר השליח "בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם", וממילא שיילינן ליה אם נכתב לשמה, והוא אומר "אין". ולקמיה מפרש מאי טעמא לא אצרכוהו נמי למימר "לשמה":
Rashi on Gittin 2b:1:1.english: Gemara: Because they are not experts in [the requirement of writing it] for her sake - The people of overseas are not Torah scholars, and they do not know that the get must be written for the sake of the woman. And a verse is written: "And he shall write for her a bill of divorce" (Deuteronomy 24:1) — "for her," meaning for her sake. Therefore the agent says, "It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence," and automatically we ask him whether it was written for her sake, and he says, "Yes." And further on [the Gemara] explains the reason why they did not require him to say "for her sake" as well.

Rashi on Gittin 2b:2:1.hebrew: לפי שאין עדים מצויין לקיימו - אין שיירות מצויות משם לכאן, שאם יבא הבעל ויערער, לומר "לא כתבתיו", שיהו עדים מצויין להכיר חתימת העדים, והאמינוהו לשליח. ולקמן פריך בין לרבא בין לרבה: ליבעי תרי:
Rashi on Gittin 2b:2:1.english: Because there are no witnesses available to ratify it - Caravans are not readily available from there to here, so that if the husband comes and contests, saying, "I did not write it," there would be witnesses available to recognize the signatures of the witnesses; therefore [the Sages] trusted the agent. And later [the Gemara] asks, according to both Rava and Rabbah: Let [the Sages] require two [witnesses]?

Rashi on Gittin 2b:3:1.hebrew: דאתיוהו בי תרי - ושניהם נעשו שלוחים לגרשה, והגט יוצא מתחת ידי שניהם. לרבה בעי למימר, לרבא לא בעי למימר, שהרי שנים הם, ואם יערער בעל, הרי הם מצויין לקיימו:
Rashi on Gittin 2b:3:1.english: Where two brought it - Both of them were made agents to divorce her, and the bill of divorce comes out from under the hands of both. According to Rabbah, it needs to be said [that they must say "in our presence it was written and in our presence it was signed"]; according to Rava, it does not need to be said, since they are two, and if the husband objects, they are available to ratify it.

Rashi on Gittin 2b:3:2.hebrew: אי נמי ממדינה למדינה בארץ ישראל - כגון יהודה וגליל. דסלקא דעתא השתא, דלא שכיחי שיירתא, לרבה דלא חייש לעירעורא דנימא מזוייף הוא — לא בעי למימר, הואיל ובקיאין כל בני ארץ ישראל לשמה. לרבא בעי למימר, דהא אין שיירות מצויות:
Rashi on Gittin 2b:3:2.english: Alternatively, from region to region in Eretz Yisrael - For example, Judea and the Galilee. For it would enter one's mind now, [seeing that] caravans are not frequent, that according to Rabba, who is not concerned about an objection, that one might say "it is forged," there is no need to say [that the bill must be ratified], since all the people of Eretz Yisrael are expert in [the requirement that it be written] for her sake. According to Rava, one would [still] need to say [so], for caravans are not frequent.

Rashi on Gittin 2b:4:1.hebrew: אי נמי באותה מדינה - כגון מעיר לעיר במדינה אחת, מדינה "רונטריד"א" בלע"ז. ובמדינת הים, לרבה בעי למימר, דהא אין בקיאין לשמה; לרבא דאמר לפי שאין וכו' ומתניתין משום ערעורא דזיוף הוא, הכא לא צריך, דהא שכיחי שיירתא:
Rashi on Gittin 2b:4:1.english: Alternatively, within that region - For example, from one city to another in one region; "region" is rontarida in the vernacular. And [if it is] in a country overseas, according to Rabbah it needs to say [that the agent must declare], since they are not experts in [the requirement that the document be written] for her sake. According to Rava, who said "because there are no..." etc., and the Mishnah [requires the declaration] because of the challenge of forgery, here it is not necessary, since caravans are common.

Rashi on Gittin 2b:5:1.hebrew: מידי דהוה אכל עדיות שבתורה - קושיא הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 2b:5:1.english: Just as is the case with all testimonies in the Torah - This is a question.

Rashi on Gittin 2b:5:2.hebrew: ומשני עד אחד נאמן באיסורין - שהרי האמינה תורה כל אחד ואחד מישראל על הפרשת תרומה, ועל השחיטה, ועל ניקור הגיד והחלב:
Rashi on Gittin 2b:5:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: One witness is deemed credible with regard to prohibitions - For the Torah entrusted every single Jew with [the separation of] teruma, with slaughter, and with the removal of the sciatic nerve and the forbidden fat.

Rashi on Gittin 2b:6:1.hebrew: דלא איתחזק איסורא - דחלב בהך חתיכה, איסורא גופא:
Rashi on Gittin 2b:6:1.english: For the prohibition has not been established as a presumption - For [the status of] forbidden fat in this piece, [that is,] the prohibited item itself.

Rashi on Gittin 2b:7:1.hebrew: הכא איתחזק - בהך איתתא איסור אשת איש. ומטבל ושחיטה לא גמרינן לה, כדאמרינן ביבמות (דף פח.), דהתם בידו לתקנן, לפיכך נאמן להעיד עליהן:
Rashi on Gittin 2b:7:1.english: Here there is a presumption - Regarding this woman, [there is a presumption of] the prohibition of a married woman. And we do not derive it [i.e., this case] from [the cases of] immersion and slaughter, as we say in Yevamot (88a), for there it is in his power to rectify them; therefore he is believed to testify about them.

Rashi on Gittin 2b:7:2.hebrew: ואין דבר ערוה - ראוי להתירו בפחות משנים. דיליף דבר דבר מממון: כתיב הכא "כי מצא בה ערות דבר" (דברים כ״ד:א׳), וכתיב התם "על פי שנים עדים יקום דבר" (שם יט), במס' סוטה (דף ג:):
Rashi on Gittin 2b:7:2.english: And there is no matter of forbidden relations - [that is] fit to be permitted by fewer than two [witnesses]. For [the Gemara] derives it by [verbal analogy of] "matter" "matter" from monetary law: Here it is written, "for he has found in her a matter of nakedness" (Deuteronomy 24:1), and there it is written, "on the testimony of two witnesses a matter shall be established" (ibid. 19:15), in tractate Sotah (page 3b).

Rashi on Gittin 2b:8:1.hebrew: רוב ישראל בקיאין הם - ואין לחושדן:
Rashi on Gittin 2b:8:1.english: Most of Israel are experts - and one should not suspect them.

Rashi on Gittin 2b:8:2.hebrew: ואפילו לר' מאיר דחייש למיעוטא - גבי קטן וקטנה: אין חולצין ולא מייבמין קטן, שמא ימצא סריס; קטנה, שמא תמצא איילונית, כו' במס' יבמות (דף קיט.):
Rashi on Gittin 2b:8:2.english: And even according to Rabbi Meir, who is concerned about a minority - In the case of a minor boy and a minor girl: "We do not perform chalitza nor yibbum with a minor boy, lest he be found to be a eunuch; [nor with] a minor girl, lest she be found to be an ayilonit [a woman incapable of bearing children]," etc., in tractate Yevamot (119a).

Rashi on Gittin 2b:8:3.hebrew: סתם ספרי דדייני - סופרי הדיינים, שרגילין לכתוב כל שטרי גיטין:
Rashi on Gittin 2b:8:3.english: Ordinary scribes of the judges - The scribes of the judges, who are accustomed to write all bills of divorce.

Rashi on Gittin 2b:8:4.hebrew: מיגמר גמירי - דגט אשה בעי לשמה:
Rashi on Gittin 2b:8:4.english: They are learned - That a woman's bill of divorce requires [being written] for her sake.

Rashi on Gittin 2b:8:5.hebrew: ורבנן הוא דאצריכו - למיחש למלתא משום דאיכא דאשכח כתוב ועומד, כגון שנכתב לשם א' מבני עירו ששמו כשמו ושמה כשמה, ונמלך מלגרש:
Rashi on Gittin 2b:8:5.english: And it is the Sages who required - to be concerned about the matter, because there is one who finds [a get] already written and standing [ready], for example, one that was written for the sake of someone from his town whose name is like his name and whose wife's name is like her name, and [that person] changed his mind about divorcing.

Tosafot on Gittin 2b:1:1.hebrew: לפי שאין בקיאין לשמה - וא"ת: מאי שנא לשמה דאין בקיאין, משאר הלכות גיטין, כגון מחובר, ושינה שמו ושמה, ונכתב ביום ונחתם בלילה? ואין לומר דנקט לשמה דשכיח טפי, דמשכח גט ששמו כשמו ושמה כשמה ומשדר לה, וגם הסופר שרגיל לכתוב טופסי גיטין אגב שיטפיה מישתלי וכתב שמו ושמה, וה"ה שאר הלכות גיטין — זה אינו; דהא אמר לקמן (גיטין דף ט:): "בג' דרכים שוו גיטי נשים לשחרורי עבדים", ופריך: "והא איכא לשמה?" בשלמא לרבה היינו מוליך ומביא, אלא לרבא קשיא. ותו, בין לרבה בין לרבא הא איכא מחובר; אלמא לרבה דוקא נקט לשמה בכלל מוליך ומביא, ולא נקט מחובר. ומפרש ר"ת דבכל הלכות גיטין בקיאין, אלא דהך דרשה דוכתב לה לשמה אינה נראית להם עיקר דרשה, ואין בקיאין פירוש: אין חוששין לדרשה דלשמה; ולאחר שלמדו דלקמן, פירוש: לאחר שקיבלוה. והא דפ"ה דממילא שיילינן ליה אי הוה לשמה ואמר אין — אין נראה, דלא משתמיט בשום דוכתא שיהא צריך לישאל; ועוד, דאם כן לימא: איכא בינייהו אם צריך לישאל. ואומר ר"י דסתמא לשמה קא מסהיד, כדפירש בקונטרס נמי בסמוך. והא דאמר לקמן: "מי קתני בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם לשמה?" — נהי דסתמא לשמה משמע, מכל מקום כיון דעיקר תקנה משום לשמה הוא, הוה ליה למימר בהדיא:
Tosafot on Gittin 2b:1:1.english: Because they are not experts in [writing it] for her sake - And if you ask: What is different about "for her sake," that they are not experts in it, as opposed to the other laws of divorce documents, such as [a get written on something] attached [to the ground], or [a get in which] he changed his name or her name, or [a get that] was written by day and signed at night? And one cannot say that [the Gemara] specified "for her sake" because it is more common — that one may find a get whose [husband's] name is the same as his name and [whose wife's] name is the same as her name, and he sends it to her; and also the scribe, who is accustomed to writing templates of divorce documents, by force of habit forgets and writes [the names in the template] "his name and her name"; and the same applies to the other laws of divorce documents — this is not [a valid answer]; for [the Gemara] says later (Gittin 9b): "In three ways, divorce documents of women are equal to the release of slaves," and it asks: "But there is also [the requirement of] 'for her sake'?" Granted, according to Rabbah, this is [included in] "carries and brings"; but according to Rava it is difficult. Furthermore, both according to Rabbah and according to Rava, there is also [the law of a get written on something] attached [to the ground]; so we see that, according to Rabbah, [the Gemara] specifically mentioned "for her sake" as part of "carries and brings," and did not mention [the law of] attached. And Rabbeinu Tam explains that in all the laws of divorce documents they are experts, but this derivation of "and he shall write for her" — "for her sake" — does not appear to them to be a primary derivation; and "they are not experts" means that they are not concerned about the derivation of "for her sake"; and ["after they learned" the matter] later means: after they accepted it. And as for what Rashi says, that we ask him of our own accord whether it was for her sake, and he says yes — this does not seem right, since nowhere is it mentioned that he needs to be asked; and furthermore, if so, let [the Gemara] say: "The difference between them is whether he needs to be asked." And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that he is testifying [that it was written] for her sake implicitly, as [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres also shortly below. And as for what [the Gemara] says later: "Does [the Mishnah] teach: 'In my presence it was written and in my presence it was signed for her sake'?" — Granted that [the wording] implies "for her sake" implicitly, nevertheless, since the main enactment is on account of "for her sake," it should have said so explicitly:

Tosafot on Gittin 2b:1:2.hebrew: לפי שאין בקיאין לשמה - קשה, דלקמן (גיטין דף ה.) תניא: הוא עצמו שהביא גיטו, אינו צריך שיאמר "בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם". מאי שנא הוא משלוחו? אי חיישינן שמא לא נעשה לשמה — וטעמא דאמר לקמן: מינקט נקט ליה בידיה, ואיהו מערער עלויה — למה לא יערער, אם מתחילה לא ידע דבעי לשמה, והשתא ידע? ואומר ר"י, דמסקינן בסמוך דרוב בקיאין הן, וסתם ספרי גמירי, וליכא אלא לעז בעלמא, דמסתמא שלא כדין יערער. והכא שמביאו הבעל בעצמו, ליכא למיחש אפילו ללעז, דתו לא מערער, כדאמר בסמוך: מנקט נקיט בידיה וכו':
Tosafot on Gittin 2b:1:2.english: Because they are not experts in [writing] it for her sake - This is difficult, for later (Gittin 5a) it was taught in a baraita: If the husband himself brought his bill of divorce, he does not need to say, "It was written in my presence and signed in my presence." What is different about him [bringing it himself] from his agent [bringing it]? If we are concerned that perhaps it was not done for her sake — and the reason stated later is: he is holding it in his hand, and he would be the one to contest it — why would he not contest it, if at first he did not know that it must be [written] for her sake, and now he knows? And Rabbi Yitzchak says: For we conclude shortly [in the Gemara] that most [scribes] are experts, and ordinary scribes have learned [the law], and there is nothing here but a mere rumor [of invalidity], since presumably, if it were improper, he would contest it. And here, where the husband himself brings it, there is no need to be concerned even about a rumor, since he will no longer contest it, as it says shortly: he is holding it in his hand, etc.:

Tosafot on Gittin 2b:3:1.hebrew: מאי בינייהו - לא מצי למימר: מוליך איכא בינייהו, דלרבה נמי, לרבנן בתראי, במוליך צ"ל "בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם", דגזרינן מוליך אטו מביא. ולת"ק נמי הוי בכלל הא דאמר "איכא בינייהו ממדינה למדינה בארץ ישראל". והא דלא קאמר "גט מקויים איכא בינייהו" - משום דהוי בכלל "דאתיוה בי תרי", דדמי למקויים:
Tosafot on Gittin 2b:3:1.english: What is the difference between them? - [The Gemara] could not have said: "A case of one who takes [the get] is the difference between them," for according to Rabbah as well, [in the view of] the later Rabbis, one who takes [a get] must also say "It was written in my presence and signed in my presence," for we decree [that the law of] one who takes [applies] because of one who brings. And according to the first Tanna as well, [this case] is included in what [the Gemara] said: "There is a difference between them [in the case of traveling] from one region to another region in Eretz Yisrael." And as for the fact that [the Gemara] did not say: "A ratified get is the difference between them" - [that is] because it is included in "where two brought it," which is similar to a ratified [get]:

Tosafot on Gittin 2b:3:2.hebrew: דאתיוה בי תרי - פ"ה למ"ד: לפי שאין עדים מצויין לקיימו, אלו יקיימוהו. וקשה: דאטו בכיפא תלו להו, שיהו מזומנין לקיימו כשיבא הבעל ויערער? ועוד: דלמה לי דאתיוה בי תרי? כך שוים שנים מן השוק שמכירין חתימת העדים. ומפרש ריב"א: דאתיוה בי תרי ואמרי שהבעל שלחם, דתו לא מהימן לומר "לא שלחתים", דהכי אמר לקמן (גיטין דף ה.): שנים אין צריכין לומר "בפני נכתב" וכו'. ומה, אילו יאמרו "בפנינו גירשה" מי לא מהימני? ולהאי לא חיישינן שמא החתים במזיד עדים פסולין, דמסתמא כיון דשלח לה גט, כדין עשאו, דאינו חשוד להכשילה:
Tosafot on Gittin 2b:3:2.english: "Where two brought it" - Rashi explains, according to the one who says [that the reason for the requirement is] that witnesses are not readily available to ratify it: [in that case, where two brought it,] these two would ratify it. But this is difficult: Are they hanging on a peg, [so to speak,] that they should be on hand to ratify it when the husband comes and objects? Furthermore, why do I need [the case where] two brought it? Any two people from the marketplace who recognize the signatures of the witnesses are just as good. And Riva explains: [The case is] where two brought it and said that the husband sent them; he is then no longer believed to say, "I did not send them," for so [the Gemara] says later (Gittin 5a): The two [agents] do not need to say, "It was written in our presence," etc. For if they were to say, "In our presence he divorced her," would they not be believed? And in this case we are not concerned lest he intentionally had invalid witnesses sign, for presumably, since he sent her a get, he made it properly, as he is not suspected of causing her to stumble.

Tosafot on Gittin 2b:5:1.hebrew: ליבעי תרי - אכתי לא ידע הא דפרישית, דלא הוי טעמא אלא משום לעז, עד לבסוף:
Tosafot on Gittin 2b:5:1.english: Let us require two - [The questioner] still did not know what I explained, that the reason is only because of a bad name (la'az), until the end [of the discussion]:

Tosafot on Gittin 2b:5:2.hebrew: מידי דהוה אכל עדיות שבתורה - בדלי"ת גרסינן, כגון עדות דיני ממונות ודיני נפשות. ואית דגריס "עריות" ברי"ש, ולא נהירא; דאם כן, מאי משני "עד אחד נאמן באיסורין"? מה לו להזכיר איסורין? והא ערוה נמי איסור הוא! והכי הוה ליה למימר: לא דמי לשאר עריות, והוה ליה ליתן טעם. ומיהו יש לומר דה"ק: עד אחד נאמן באיסורין להתיר, והא דבעי תרי — הני מילי לאסור, דחד לאו כל כמיניה. אבל הא דקאמר "כל עריות" לא אתי שפיר, דמאי "כל"? עיקר דבר שבערוה אין פחות משנים — זהו באשת איש, בגיטין ובקידושין, וזנות דאשת איש לאוסרה על בעלה:
Tosafot on Gittin 2b:5:2.english: "Just as is the case with all testimonies in the Torah" - We read [eduyot] with a dalet, for example, testimony in monetary cases and in capital cases. But there are those who read arayot ["forbidden sexual relations"] with a resh, and this does not seem right; for if so, what is the answer "One witness is deemed credible with regard to prohibitions"? Why did it need to mention prohibitions? Surely a forbidden sexual relation is also a prohibition! Rather, it should have said: It is not like the other forbidden sexual relations, and it would have given a reason. However, one can say that this is what [the Gemara] means: One witness is deemed credible with regard to prohibitions, to permit; and as for the fact that it requires two, that applies to prohibiting, for one [witness] is not authorized [to do so]. But what [the Gemara] says, "all forbidden sexual relations," does not fit well, for what is "all"? The essential principle, that in a matter of forbidden relations [there must be] no fewer than two [witnesses], this is with regard to a married woman, in divorce and betrothal and licentiousness of a married woman, to prohibit her to her husband.

Tosafot on Gittin 2b:5:3.hebrew: עד אחד נאמן באיסורין - פי' הקונטרס: שהרי האמינה תורה כל אחד ואחד על הפרשת תרומה, ושחיטה, וניקור הגיד, וחלב. ולא היה לו להזכיר הפרשת תרומה ושחיטה, דבהנהו נאמן אע"ג דאיתחזק איסורא, משום דבידו לתקנם, כמו שפ"ה בסמוך; והכי אמר בהאשה רבה (יבמות דף פח.). ושחיטה, אע"ג דהשתא אין בידו לתקנו, מעיקרא היה בידו לשחוט; דאם לא כן, אמאי מהימן כיון דאיתחזק איסורא? דלא מצינו בשום מקום שיצטרך בגדול אחד עומד על גביו, ומעשים בכל יום דמהימן. אע"ג דלא שייך "רוב מצויין" אצל שחיטה "מומחין הן", כגון שנחתך כל הראש ואין בית השחיטה ניכר. ומה שאנו סומכין על הנשים בשחיטה, אע"פ שאין יודעות הלכות שחיטה, כיון שבידה ללמוד לשחוט, או להשכיר אחרים שישחטו לה — כבידה דמי. וא"ת: ומנא לן דעד אחד נאמן באיסורין? וי"ל: דילפינן מנדה, דדרשינן בפרק המדיר (כתובות דף עב.): "וספרה לה" — לעצמה. וא"ת: אם כן, אפילו איתחזק איסורא? וי"ל: דאינה בחזקת שתהא רואה כל שעה, וכשעברו שבעה טהורה ממילא, ולא איתחזק איסורא, וגם בידה לטבול:
Tosafot on Gittin 2b:5:3.english: One witness is deemed credible with regard to prohibitions - Rashi explained: For the Torah entrusted each and every person with the separation of terumah, with slaughter, and with removing the sciatic nerve and the forbidden fat. [But Rashi] should not have mentioned the separation of terumah and slaughter, for with regard to those he is believed even though a prohibition has been established [on the item], because it is in his power to rectify them, as Rashi explains shortly below; and so it says in the chapter HaIsha Rabba (Yevamot 88a). And as for slaughter, even though now it is not in his power to rectify it, originally it was in his power to slaughter; for if not, why is he believed, since a prohibition has been established? For we do not find anywhere that it is necessary for an adult to stand over [the slaughterer], and it is a daily occurrence that he is believed. [This is so] even though the principle that "most of those commonly found are experts" is not applicable to slaughter, for example where the entire head was cut off and the place of slaughter is not recognizable. And as for the fact that we rely on women for slaughter, even though they do not know the laws of slaughter, since it is in her power to learn to slaughter, or to hire others to slaughter for her, it is considered as being in her power. And if you ask: From where do we know that one witness is believed with regard to prohibitions? One can answer: We derive it from a niddah, as we expound in the chapter HaMadir (Ketubot 72a): "And she shall count for herself" — for herself. And if you ask: If so, [he should be believed] even where a prohibition has been established? One can answer: She is not in the presumptive state of seeing [blood] at every moment, and when the seven days have passed she becomes pure automatically, so a prohibition has not been established; and also, it is in her power to immerse.

Tosafot on Gittin 2b:5:4.hebrew: עד אחד נאמן באיסורין - הקשה ר"ת: מה תשובה היא זאת? עיקר הגט יוכיח שצריך לחותמו בשנים! ותי' דה"ק: דעד אחד נאמן באיסורין בכה"ג, שעיקר הגט נעשה כבר, ושוב אין צריך אלא גילוי מילתא לידע אם לשמה נכתב:
Tosafot on Gittin 2b:5:4.english: One witness is deemed credible with regard to prohibitions - Rabbeinu Tam asked: What kind of answer is this? The essential [part of the] bill of divorce proves [otherwise], for it must be signed by two [witnesses]! And he answered that this is what [the Gemara] is saying: One witness is deemed credible with regard to prohibitions in a case such as this, where the essential [part of the] bill of divorce has already been done, and nothing further is needed except the revealing of the matter, to know whether it was written for her sake:

Tosafot on Gittin 2b:7:1.hebrew: הוי דבר שבערוה - האי דנקט "דבר שבערוה", אומר ר"י: משום דבהאשה רבה (יבמות דף פח.) בשאר איסורי, כגון טבל והקדש וקונמות, מספקא לן אי מהימן אפילו איתחזק איסורא ולאו בידו, או לא. וא"ת: אי עד אחד נאמן בשאר איסורין אפילו איתחזק איסורא ולאו בידו, אמאי איצטריך "וספרה לה לעצמה"? ויש לומר: דס"ד דחשיב כמו דבר שבערוה:
Tosafot on Gittin 2b:7:1.english: It is a matter of forbidden sexual relations - As for the fact that [the Gemara] specified "a matter of forbidden sexual relations," the Ri says: [It is] because in Ha'isha Rabba (Yevamot 88a), regarding other prohibitions, such as tevel (untithed produce), hekdesh (consecrated property), and konamot (vows), we are uncertain whether he is believed, even where the prohibition was established and it is not in his control, or not. And if you say: If a single witness is believed regarding other prohibitions even where the prohibition was established and it is not in his control, why was it necessary [for the verse to say] "and she shall count for herself"? One can answer: [It is] because one might have thought that it is considered like a matter of forbidden sexual relations.

Tosafot on Gittin 2b:8:1.hebrew: סתם ספרי דדייני מיגמר גמירי - והוי כמו מיעוטא דמיעוטא, דלא חיישינן אפילו לרבי מאיר:
Tosafot on Gittin 2b:8:1.english: Ordinary judicial scribes are learned in this - And it is like a minority of a minority, about which we are not concerned even according to Rabbi Meir:

Tosafot on Gittin 2b:8:2.hebrew: ורבנן הוא דאצרוך - פירש בקונטרס: משום דאיכא דאשכח כתוב ועומד, כגון שנכתב לשם א' מבני עירו ששמו כשמו, ונמלך מלגרש. וקשה, דבהוחזק שני יוסף בן שמעון אפילו נכתב לשמו פסול לגרש בו לר' מאיר, כדאמרינן בריש כל הגט (לקמן גיטין דף כד:): "כתב לגרש בו את הגדולה לא יגרש בו את הקטנה", וקאמר בגמ': "קטנה הוא דלא מצי מגרש, הא גדולה מגרש"; מוקי לה כר' אלעזר ולא כר"מ, משום דבעינן שיהא מוכיח מתוך עדי החתימה הי מינייהו מגרשה. ובסמוך בעי לאוקומי מתני' כר"מ, ואפילו לרבי אלעזר צריך עדי מסירה שידעו שעשאו הבעל שליח, וליכא. ואור"י דהא דאצרוך רבנן הכא, היינו כדי שלא יערער הבעל ויאמר שכתבו הסופר כדי להתלמד, והוא החתים עליו עדים, שהוא לא היה בקי לשמה:
Tosafot on Gittin 2b:8:2.english: “And it is the Sages who required [it]” - Rashi explained in the Kuntres: Because there are cases where one finds [a bill of divorce] already written and standing, for example, one that was written for one of the townspeople whose name is the same as his, and he changed his mind about divorcing. But this is difficult: where it is established that there are two people named Yosef ben Shimon, even if [the bill] was written for his name, it is invalid to divorce with it according to Rabbi Meir, as we say in the beginning of chapter Kol HaGet (below, Gittin 24b): “If he wrote [a bill] to divorce the older [wife] with it, he may not divorce the younger one with it.” And the Gemara says: “It is only the younger one that he cannot divorce with it, but the older one he can divorce [with it].” It establishes this [ruling] according to Rabbi Elazar and not according to Rabbi Meir, because we require that it be evident from the signature witnesses which of the two he is divorcing. And shortly afterward [the Gemara] wants to establish the Mishnah according to Rabbi Meir, and even according to Rabbi Elazar one needs witnesses of delivery, who know that the husband appointed him as an agent, and there are none. And the Ri says that what the Rabbis required here is so that the husband should not contest and say that the scribe wrote it in order to practice, and that he [only] had witnesses sign on it, [and] that [the scribe] was not expert in [writing it] for her sake.
